correctness.rationale: Spectral projections give each offdiagonal entry as a positive factor times a+bR(t), with a>0 and monotone decreasing R; this yields exact unique entry cutoffs and their supremum for arbitrary countable index sets. Three explicit orthogonal eigendirections give the finite example; normalized pairwise antisymmetric spectral projectors give the infinite cutoff. Four distinct spectral values of the positive definite path matrix yield sign obstructions in (0,1) and (1,2) by even functional calculus and third divided differences; established critical-exponent theorem supplies t>=2. Critical finite algebra checked in the standalone program. No numerical experiment is used for any universal step.

originality.rationale: The new statement classifies positivity-time sets by spectral cardinality for bounded real self-adjoint semigroups on finite/countable coordinate Hilbert spaces with an explicit endpoint, finite and infinite realizability, and a four-spectral obstruction. The principal established neighboring theorems concern eventual positivity/growth bounds or DN powers in finite dimension, rather than the above spectral-cardinality classification. Full-text access limitations and possible unindexed elementary analogues are recorded.
residual_risks: The full texts of the 2026 Arnold and Dobrick manuscripts could not be inspected, so the two abstract-based exclusions are not comprehensive.
An elementary equivalent finite-spectrum matrix-power argument could exist outside the indexed/inspected literature.
The four-level example uses an established critical-exponent theorem; its late-time fact is not itself claimed to be new.

value.rationale: A structurally motivated sharp threshold at three eigenvalues prevents disconnected positive-operator times in any countable dimension. Its exact formula provides every coordinate cutoff, a complete global invariant and realizability of all finite/extended cutoffs; the bounded infinite example explains how pointwise entry recovery fails to give any globally positive time. A four-level witness shows why the theorem cannot extend one level further. The result is a classification and obstruction, not a routine numerical improvement.
